```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 6,
  dpi = 80
)
```

```{r setup}
library(ggcordist)
```

ggcordist implements the four-layer display of Tokuda, Goodrich, Van Mechelen,
Gelman and Tuerlinckx, *Visualizing Distributions of Covariance Matrices*,
for draws of a covariance or correlation matrix, for example from a Stan fit.

1. histograms of `log(sd)` and of a correlation,
2. scatterplots of pairs of log standard deviations and correlations,
3. equiprobability ellipses of a bivariate normal with the sampled 2 x 2
   covariance,
4. effective variance and effective dependence.

Draws in the lowest and highest 5% of effective dependence are coloured blue
and red in every panel.

## Reference distributions

The package ships samplers for the distributions in the paper, which are
useful as priors to compare against. An inverse-Wishart with `df = k + 1` and
identity scale (the paper's Figure 1):

```{r iw}
set.seed(1234)
iw <- r_inv_wishart(1000, k = 4)
iw
plot_tableau(iw)
```

Each correlation is marginally uniform, but the joint distribution piles up in
the corners of the support, and large standard deviations go with extreme
correlations.

A separation-strategy prior with an LKJ(1) correlation matrix and half-normal
standard deviations behaves quite differently:

```{r lkj}
sep <- r_separation(1000, k = 4, cor_dist = "lkj", eta = 1)
plot_tableau(sep)
```

## Your own Stan fit

`as_cov_draws()` converts the matrix parameters of a Stan fit. For a model
with parameters `Omega` (a correlation matrix) and `tau` (a vector of scales):

```{r stan, eval = FALSE}
fit <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model("model.stan")$sample(data = stan_data)

post <- as_cov_draws(fit, par = "Omega", type = "cor", sd_par = "tau")
plot_tableau(post)
```

The same call works for `rstan::stanfit` objects and for `posterior` draws.
Use `type = "cov"` for a covariance matrix parameter, or `"chol_cor"` and
`"chol_cov"` for Cholesky factors. For `brms`, name the grouping factor:

```{r brms, eval = FALSE}
post <- as_cov_draws(brms_fit, group = "subject")
```

The paper's grid assumes exchangeable variables, so one panel per type of pair
suffices. Posterior draws usually are not exchangeable: choose which variables
to show with `idx`, or look at every pair:

```{r pairs}
plot_tableau(iw, idx = c(2, 3, 4, 1))
plot_pairs(r_inv_wishart(500, k = 3))
```

## Prior versus posterior

`plot_compare()` overlays several sets of draws.

```{r compare}
plot_compare(list(
  `LKJ(1)` = r_lkj(1000, k = 3, eta = 1),
  `LKJ(10)` = r_lkj(1000, k = 3, eta = 10)
))
```

## Other displays

```{r other}
plot_ellipses(iw, i = 1, j = 2)
plot_effective(r_lkj(1000, k = 20))
plot_eigen(r_lkj(500, k = 5))
```

`plot_cor3d()` draws the three-dimensional scatterplot of three correlations
with `rgl` (not run here).
